title: Sampling Switches
intro: Switched-capacitor circuits sample voltages on capacitors with MOS switches. The switch's imperfections set their accuracy.

items: On-resistance Ron: with sampling capacitance C the sampling bandwidth is 1/(2*pi*Ron*C). To settle to N bits takes t = (N + 1) * ln(2) * Ron * C.

Charge injection: when the switch turns off, its channel charge W*L*Cox*Vov is split between the source and the capacitor, creating an error voltage on the capacitor. Reduce it with small switches, dummy devices or bottom-plate sampling.
Clock feedthrough: overlap capacitance couples the clock edge onto the sampled node.
Nonlinear Ron: Ron depends on the input voltage through VGS - VTH, making the sampling distortion signal-dependent. Bootstrapped switches keep VGS constant.

blocks.alt: A sampling switch controlled by a clock connects the input Vin to the output node Vout. A hold capacitor CH connects from the output node to ground.
blocks.caption: A switch and a capacitor make the simplest sample-and-hold circuit.

blocks.text: A transmission gate (NMOS plus PMOS in parallel) keeps Ron lower over the signal range, and its charge injection partly cancels.

blocks.title: Settling time
blocks.text: A sampling switch has Ron = 1 kohm driving C = 1 pF. How long to settle to within half an LSB of a 10-bit converter?
solution: Error below 1/2 LSB of 10 bits means exp(-t/tau) < 2^-11, so t = 11 * ln 2 * tau = 7.6 ns.

blocks.title: Switch noise
blocks.text: What noise voltage is sampled on C = 1 pF, regardless of Ron?
solution: kT/C noise: sqrt(kT/C) = 64 uV rms at 300 K.
